s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic skin eruption with atypical lymphocytic infiltrate
salient_findings: Multiple erythematous and violaceous plaques and nodules on the buttocks
Atypical lymphocytic infiltrate in the dermis with eosinophils and plasma cells
key_facts: Male patient in his 70s
Eruption duration of 5 years
Previous treatments with oral antibiotics, oral doxepin, and UV-B phototherapy failed
History of HSV-2 infection on the buttocks
Negative syphilis screen
Molecular analysis showed a weak clonal band in a polyclonal background initially, but no clonal rearrangement on repeat
Biopsy showed dense infiltrate of atypical CD4+ small to medium-sized lymphocytes
Epidermotropism was not identified in the first biopsy, but present in the second
Lesions are smooth and firm
Located on the superior buttocks and intergluteal cleft bilaterally

shortlist: Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium-sized pleomorphic T-cell lymphoma

shortlist.label: Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium-sized pleomorphic T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the biopsy findings of atypical CD4+ small to medium-sized lymphocytes and the clinical presentation of persistent skin eruption

shortlist.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with the chronic skin eruption and atypical lymphocytic infiltrate, although less specific than the primary cutaneous CD4+ lymphoma

shortlist.label: Mycosis fungoides
shortlist.why_kept: A common form of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma that could present with similar skin lesions, but the absence of epidermotropism in the initial biopsy makes it less likely

shortlist.label: Lymphomatoid papulosis
shortlist.why_kept: Could be considered due to the presence of atypical lymphocytes, but the clinical presentation and biopsy findings are not as typical for this condition

shortlist.label: Cutaneous pseudolymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Remains a possibility given the history of HSV-2 infection and the presence of atypical lymphocytes, but the persistent nature of the eruption and specific biopsy findings make lymphoma more likely

s4.champion: Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium-sized pleomorphic T-cell lymphoma

raw.champion: Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium-sized pleomorphic T-cell lymphoma
raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of multiple erythematous and violaceous plaques and nodules with a dense infiltrate of atypical CD4+ small to medium-sized lymphocytes in the dermis, along with the history of previous treatments failing and the specific location of the lesions, supports this diagnosis. The molecular analysis initially showing a weak clonal band also leans towards a lymphoma diagnosis, although the repeat study showed no clonal rearrangement.

rejected.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: Too broad, as it encompasses several subtypes, including the champion diagnosis

rejected.label: Mycosis fungoides
rejected.why: Typically presents with epidermotropism and Pautrier's microabscesses, which were not consistently found in this case

rejected.label: Lymphomatoid papulosis
rejected.why: Characterized by a more benign course with spontaneous regression of lesions, which does not fit the patient's 5-year duration of eruption

rejected.label: Cutaneous pseudolymphoma
rejected.why: Usually associated with a known antigenic trigger and a more polymorphic infiltrate, which does not align with the patient's history of HSV-2 infection and the specific biopsy findings
